JUDGMENT

This petition is filed by the petitioners U/S 22 of Employees Compensation Act, 1923 seeking compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- with interest in respect of death of one Sharath Babu.N @ Sharath Kumar.N in the above case.
2. It is the case of petitioners that, Sharath Babu.N @ Sharath Kumar.N is the husband of the 1 st petitioner and father of the 2nd petitioner and son of the 3 rd and 4th petitioners.

That he was working as a driver under the 1 st respondent in Canter bearing Reg.No.KA-40-3908 on a salary of Rs.20,000/- per month and Batta of Rs.200/- per day and that the deceased use to work all the days in a month and in all used to earn a sum of Rs.26,200/- per month including batta.

That while Sharath Babu was during and in course of employment with the 1 st respondent as a driver in Canter bearing Reg.No.KA-40-3908 SBS met with an incident on 12.11.2021 at about 4.00 pm at Udamalodu, Gowribidanur Taluk.
That while he was driving the canter, an electric wire touched to the canter, as a result he sustained burning injuries and he succumbed to the said injuries.

Post mortem was conducted at General hospital, Gowribidanur and the dead body was handed over to the petitioners and they have spent a sum of Rs.1,50,000/- towards transportation of dead body,
funeral and obsequies etc.
That a case has been registered by Gowribidanur Rural Police in Crime No.306/2021 u/Sec 304(A) of IPC.

Bhavani D.B vs Srinivasa.N on 2 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44627120/
2 (SCCH-12) 4 ECA No.62/2022 3.
That deceased was aged about 27 years at the time of accident and he was hale and healthy.
Petitioners have lost love and affection and all of them were depending upon the income of the deceased.
That deceased was an employee under 1 st respondent as a driver of Canter bearing Reg.No.KA-40-3908 and due to his death, petitioners are put to untold hardship, mental agony.
That he died during the course of his employment under the 1st respondent and the 2nd respondent is the insurer of the said canter.
Hence both respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
On all these grounds they prayed to allow the petition and award compensation as prayed.
4. In pursuance of notice respondents appeared through their counsel and filed objections separately.

The respondent no.1 in his written statement contended that he is the R.C owner of Canter bearing Reg.No.KA-40-3908 and the said vehicle has been duly insured with 2nd respondent as on the date of accident.
Further he denied the relationship of the deceased with the petitioners.

Further he admitted that deceased Sharath Babu.N was working as a driver under this respondent in Canter bearing Reg.No.KA-40-3908 on a salary of Rs.20,000/- per month and met with an incident as alleged in the petition.
Further he denied petitioners have spent Rs.1,50,000/- towards transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies etc.
He admitted that the deceased was died during and in the course of employment with this respondent as a (SCCH-12) 5 ECA No.62/2022 driver in Canter bearing Reg.No.KA-40-3908.
On all these grounds prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. The respondent no.2 in his written statement has contended that the petition filed by the petitioners is not maintainable either in law or on facts and this court has no jurisdiction since the accident occurred at Gowribidanur taluk, Chikkaballapur District and as per petition the petitioners were ordinary resident of Sidlaghatta taluk, Chikkaballapur district and R.C owner of the vehicle is resident of Shidlaghatta Taluk
hence, the petition is liable to be dismissed for want of jurisdiction.

That this respondent has issued policy to Canter bearing Reg.No.KA- 40-3908 and liability to indemnify the 1 st respondent is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy provisions of M.V.
Act

valid and effective driving license held by the driver of Canter goods vehicle, valid R.C and F.C,
pollution certificate, valid permit and subject to confirmation of Section 64VB of Insurance Act.
This respondent seeks protection under Section 147 and 149(2) of M.V.Act.
That the police authorities have not filed the charge sheet against the driver or owner of the vehicle.
Deceased Sharath Babu was not an employee under the accused no.1 and 2 so there is no employee and employer relationship between them.
The police have not complied provisions of Sec.158(6) of M.V.Act.

Age,
occupation, income and manner of death is denied.
On all these grounds he prayed to dismiss the petition.
Since charge sheet is filed against the school headmaster, on the application filed by 2nd respondent, the school headmaster, Umbalagolu school is impleaded as respondent no.3.

On Bhavani D.B vs Srinivasa.N on 2 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44627120/
3 10.12.2024 he filed memo to treat his objection to I.A under Order 1 Rule 10 of CPC as his objection to main petition also.
The said memo is accepted.
In his objections he contended that, petition is not maintainable and on the date of accident school was opened, school staff and children were also present.
On that day there was heavy rain in the school premises and in the entire Gouribidanur taluk.

BEO had directed the school to be closed on 12.11.2021 due to heavy rain and as such informing the SDMC resident and members the school head master declared the holiday in the afternoon session, as such it was declared holiday after 2.30pm and school was closed.
At that time Sharath Babu came to school premises for supplying food to school children.
His death is not informed to school staff and due to power line touch to the canter lorry he died on the spot.
The FIR is registered against the head master and CEO of KPTCL, but after investigation charge sheet is filed only against the school master by leaving the name of CEO, KPTCL.
Police have not correctly investigated the case as school head master and staff were not at the spot but charge sheet is still filed against the school master for negligence.
The criminal case is pending in Gouribidanur court and this case is not maintainable.
On all these grounds he prayed to dismiss the petition.

. On the basis of the above pleadings, following issues are framed;
ISSUES
1. Whether the Petitioners prove that they are the L.R's of the deceased Sharath Babu and competent persons to file the above petition?
2. Whether the Petitioners prove that Sharath Babu was working under the 1st respondent as driver?
3. Whether the petitioners proves that, the accident dated 12.11.2021 has occurred during the course of employment of the deceased as alleged?

4. Whether the petitioners prove that Sharath Babu.N was driving the Canter bearing No.KA- 40-3908 at Udamalodu Govt. Higher primary school campus and the canter touched the electric wire and he sustained burning injuries and died as alleged?
5. Whether the petitioner prove the age, occupation, income of deceased and their permanent dependency?
6.

In order to prove the above issues the petitioner got examined as P.W.1. Through her Ex. P1 to 13 documents are marked.
She is fully cross examined by respondent no.2.
Ont (SCCH-12) 8 ECA No.62/2022 he other hand, 3rd respondent by name Balappa.N, School Head Master, Udamalodu got examined as R.W.1.
No document is marked on his behalf.
Administrative officer of 2 nd respondent insurance company is examined as R.W.2.
Through him Ex.R.1 and 2 documents are marked and respondent side evidence is closed.
9. I have heard the arguments of both sides and perused the entire materials placed on record and my answers on the above issues are as follows;

ISSUE No.1 : In the Affirmative,
 ISSUE No.2,3 & 4 : In the Affirmative,
 ISSUE No.5 : Partly in the Affirmative,
 ISSUE No.6 : In the Affirmative,
 ISSUE No.7 : Partly in the Affirmative,
 ISSUE No.8 :
As per final order  for the following  REASONS 10. ISSUE NO. 6 :- Since this issue is on the point of jurisdiction, the same is taken first for discussion.

2nd respondent insurance company in its written statement contended that this court has no jurisdiction to entertain the case as place of accident, residents of petitioners and owner of the lorry is not within the jurisdiction of this court.
To prove that this court has no jurisdiction to entertain the above petition, authorized representative is examined as R.W.2.
Further as per the cause title and evidence of P.W.1 she is said to be resident of Bengaluru also.
Her residential address is not disputed by 2nd respondent in her cross examination.
Therefore, in the opinion of this court objection on jurisdiction is not acceptable.
Accordingly, I answer this Issue in the Negative.
11. ISSUE NO. 1 :- To prove that they are the L.Rs of deceased Sharath Babu, 1st petitioner entered witness box and he reiterated petition averments in her chief examination.
She has produced aadhaar card of petitioners at Ex.P.7 to 11 and D.L of the deceased at Ex.P.12.
They show that deceased is son of Narasimha murthy, who is petitioner no.4 and petitioner no.1 is his wife, 2 is his son and 3 is his mother.
In the evidence of P.W.1 she stated about the relation ship and also produced marriage card at Ex.P.15.
It shows that she is the wife of the deceased.
In cross examination of P.W.1 she denied that she is not the wife of deceased.
To disprove her contention and documentary evidence no contrary evidence is produced.
Therefore, in the opinion of this court petitioners have proved that they are the L.Rs of deceased.
Accordingly, this issue is answered in the Affirmative.

Bhavani D.B vs Srinivasa.N on 2 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44627120/
5 12.
ISSUE NO. 2, 3 AND 4 :-
2nd respondent disputed that deceased was working with 1st respondent and also disputed the accident occurred during the course of employment due to burning injuries.
But, 1st respondent himself filed his written statement admitted that the deceased was employed under him and he died during the course of employment.

He also submitted that,
deceased for working for salary of Rs.20,000/- per month and died during the course of employment.
But R-1 has not appeared to give evidence in the above case.
Petitioners (SCCH-12) 10 ECA No.62/2022 contended that deceased was working under the 1st respondent.
In the police record it is mentioned that deceased was working as driver in Annapoorneshwari Transport.
1st respondent has not disputed the relationship of employer and employee.
2 nd respondent also not got summoned 1st respondent to prove this fact by producing documents.
But, admission in pleadings has to be considered by the court in the absence of any contrary evidence.
Therefore, in the opinion of this court petitioners have proved that deceased was working under 1st respondent as driver and he died during the course of employment on 12.11.2021.
Hence, I answer these issues in the Affirmative.
13. ISSUE NO. 5 :- 2nd respondent disputed age, occupation and income of the deceased.
He also disputed the dependency of the petitioners on the deceased.
To prove the age petitioners have produced police documents in which, age of the deceased is mentioned as 27 years.
In petition also it is stated that deceased was aged 27 years.
They have produced his aadhaar card and D.L at Ex.P.11 and 12.
They show that he was born on 04.10.1993 and as per aadhaar card on 04.02.1993 as per D.L.
Since D.L was issued much prior to the accident.
Date mentioned in the same has to be considered.
Accident took place on 12.11.2021.
Therefore, age of the deceased as on the date of accident was 28 years.
Therefore, in the opinion of this court, age of the deceased is held as 28 years at the time of accident.

14. In respect of income of the deceased, petitioners have not produced any document, however 1st respondent employer (SCCH-12) 11 ECA No.62/2022 stated in his written statement that per month deceased was earning Rs.20,000/-.
According to petitioners deceased was earning Rs.20,000/- pe month with Batta of Rs.200/- per day and in total Rs.26,200/- was earned by him per month.
But to prove this fact no documentary evidence is available.

When income is not proved, in the opinion of this court notification issued by Govt. of India, Department of Labour and Employment dt.
03.01.2020 in which the wages is enhanced to Rs.15,000/- per month has to be considered.
The accident took place after the date of said notification.
Therefore, it has to be made applicable to the present case.
Hence, income of the deceased is considered as Rs.15,000/- per month.

15. In respect of dependency, 1st petitioner being wife and 2nd petitioner being son, 3rd and 4th petitioner being parents all of them will have to be considered as dependents of deceased as the deceased was earning member of the family.
Hence, the above issue is held Partly in the Affirmative.
16. ISSUE NO.7:
In view of above reasons petitioners are entitled for compensation.
1st respondent being employer is liable to pay compensation to the family of the deceased.
2 nd respondent being insurance company having admitted the policy is liable to indemnify 1 st respondent in payment of compensation.

Bhavani D.B vs Srinivasa.N on 2 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44627120/
6 17.

The quantum of compensation is that as per Section 4(1A) of E.C. Act where death results from the injury an amount equal to 50% of the monthly wages of the deceased (employee) (SCCH-12) 12 ECA No.62/2022 multiplied by the relevant factor or an amount of Rs.1,20,000/- whichever is more has to be taken as amount of compensation.

50% of the monthly wages of the deceased is Rs.7,500/-
and age of the deceased at the time of death was 27 years.
The relevant factor as per Schedule IV to the age group of 27 years is 213.57.
Hence, the total loss of income is Rs.7,500/- X Factor 213.57 is Rs. 16,01,775/-.
According to petitioners they have spent Rs.1,50,000/- towards transportation of dead body and funeral expenses, but no documents are produced to that effect.
However, in the opinion of this court for funeral expenses Rs.10,000/- has to be awarded.
Accordingly, the total compensation payable to family of the deceased is Rs.16,11,775/- .
All the petitioners being family members equally affected by the death of the earning member of the family entitled to share the compensation equally in the apportionment of 25:25:25:25.
Hence, I answer Issue No.6 Partly in the Affirmative.
18. ISSUE NO.8 :

In view of the above discussion on Issue No.1 to 6, I proceed to pass the following,
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners U/sec. 22 of the Employee's Compensation Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.16,11,775/- along with interest at the rate of 12% p.a. from the date of accident till the date of payment.
(SCCH-12) 13 ECA No.62/2022 Respondent no.1 being principal employer is liable to pay aforesaid amount of compensation with interest to petitioners.

In view of valid insurance as on the date of accident Respondent no.2 insurance company is liable to indemnify the principle employer and hereby directed to pay compensation to petitioners within 2 months from the date of this order.

On such deposit petitioner No. 1 to 4 are entitled to share the compensation equally in the apportionment of 25:25:25:25 and petitioner No. 1, 3 and 4 are entitled to have release of entire portion of their compensation without making F.D. Petitioner no.2 being minor, entire portion of his compensation shall be kept in F.D in any nationalized bank of the choice of his guardian till he attains the age of majority.
Office is directed to collect the bank details of petitioners and release the compensation amount by way of Electronic mode of payment i.e., RTGS/NEFT to the account of the petitioners respectively.
Case against Respondent no.3 is dismissed.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs. 1,000/-.
Draw Award Accordingly.

18. ISSUE NO.8 :
In view of the above discussion on Issue No.1 to 6, I proceed to pass the following,
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners U/sec. 22 of the Employee's Compensation Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.16,11,775/- along with interest at the rate of 12% p.a. from the date of accident till the date of payment.
(SCCH-12) 13 ECA No.62/2022 Respondent no.1 being principal employer is liable to pay aforesaid amount of compensation with interest to petitioners.
In view of valid insurance as on the date of accident Respondent no.2 insurance company is liable to indemnify the principle employer and hereby directed to pay compensation to petitioners within 2 months from the date of this order.
On such deposit petitioner No. 1 to 4 are entitled to share the compensation equally in the apportionment of 25:25:25:25 and petitioner No. 1, 3 and 4 are entitled to have release of entire portion of their compensation without making F.D. Petitioner no.2 being minor, entire portion of his compensation shall be kept in F.D in any nationalized bank of the choice of his guardian till he attains the age of majority.
Office is directed to collect the bank details of petitioners and release the compensation amount by way of Electronic mode of payment i.e., RTGS/NEFT to the account of the petitioners respectively.
Case against Respondent no.3 is dismissed.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs. 1,000/-.
Draw Award Accordingly.
